title: TypeScript SDK: cross-consumable stream outputs (AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams)
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Deliver a single, ergonomic TypeScript SDK surface that makes stream-producing APIs interoperable between AsyncIterator consumers and Web Streams consumers while preserving backpressure semantics, retry safety, and TypeScript ergonomics.

Background: We currently expose streaming outputs in a few different shapes across the SDK: AsyncIterator for Node-centric codepaths and ReadableStream/Web Stream for browser- and web-platform consumers. This fragmentation forces users to write glue code and increases docs/support burden. Prior work (ENG-6183, ENG-9142) explored bridges and unified consumer APIs but left gaps around backpressure, cancel semantics, and idempotent retries.

Scope: Implement a lightweight adapter layer that: (1) returns a small union/overload for streaming endpoints (AsyncIterable<T> | ReadableStream<T>) with stable typing, (2) provides helper shims to convert between AsyncIterator <-> Web Stream with correct cancellation semantics, (3) ensures retry and resume behavior is explicit and safe (idempotency hooks and a small retry adapter), (4) ships ergonomic examples and tests for Node (stream.pipeline compatibility) and browser (Response.body pipeTo / ReadableStreamDefaultReader).

Non-goals: We will not attempt to fully polyfill Streams API in Node <18 or rework server SDK internals. This ticket focuses on the SDK surface and adapter utilities; heavy runtime changes remain for a follow-up if needed.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a single documented streaming surface for text/chat endpoints that TypeScript narrows to AsyncIterable<T> when used in Node and to ReadableStream<T> when used in browser bundlers
Adapter utils provided: asyncIteratorToReadableStream(iterator, options), readableStreamToAsyncIterator(stream, options)
Adapters preserve cancellation: downstream cancel/return triggers upstream cancellation callback exactly once
Adapters propagate backpressure so producers yield only as consumer demands
Retry helper ensures idempotent resume where backend provides resume tokens; tests simulate partial failures and assert no duplication
Comprehensive unit and integration tests for Node (pipe/stream.pipeline) and browser-like ReadableStream reader usage
Documentation pages with copy/paste examples for common patterns and a short migration guide
Performance regression within +/-5% for p95 token latency on a representative streaming workload (verified in CI benchmarks)
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter converters and cancellation behavior; integration tests against local dev server that emits chunked tokens and supports a resume token handshake. Add E2E tests in CI: spawn Node consumer using for await..of and browser-like consumer using ReadableStreamDefaultReader; assert token order, no duplication, and correct cancellation. Add property-based tests for backpressure (consumer delays). CI also runs a perf microbenchmark to ensure p95 token latency within target.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions: prefer a tiny, dependency-free implementation using native async iterators + ReadableStream constructors (polyfilled only in test matrix where needed). Provide options object to adapters allowing a cancel callback hook and an idempotency token extractor used by retry helper. For Node consumer ergonomics, add a thin wrapper that implements node:stream.Readable.from(asyncIterable) compatibility. Avoid shipping a runtime polyfill; instead document Node compatibility matrix.

Trade-offs: Keeping adapters minimal reduces bundle size but forces some duplication in example code. Full polyfill would increase compatibility but is out of scope.

Implementation steps: 1) spec and TS types, 2) implement converters and retry helper, 3) write unit tests, 4) integration tests and perf harness, 5) docs and examples, 6) code review and rollout behind feature flag.

Open questions: How to best type the union return without harming inference for generics? We propose overloads on the method signatures returning AsyncIterable<T> for Node target builds and ReadableStream<T> for DOM target builds; runtime returned object will implement both shapes where possible.
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag (sdk.streamingAdapters=true). Default behavior for existing users remains unchanged. Gradual rollout: enable for internal Canary orgs -> beta customers -> GA. Monitor error rates, token duplication alerts, and customer support channels for 2 weeks after GA. Provide migration guide and deprecation timeline if we remove older surfaces.
comments: 2025-02-18 Asha Menon: Initial ticket created with proposed surface and trade-offs. Assigned to Diego. Added ENG-6183 and ENG-9142 as context dependencies.

2025-02-22 Diego Ramirez: Implemented first draft of readableStreamToAsyncIterator and asyncIteratorToReadableStream in feature branch. Observed cancellation fired twice when consumer calls reader.cancel + iterator.return; investigating dedup logic.

2025-02-24 Priya Shah (review): Left feedback on types — prefer overloads instead of union types to surface correct inference for generic consumers. Also asked for explicit examples for node:stream compatibility.
2025-02-26 Diego Ramirez: Fixed double-cancel by adding an internal 'cancelled' flag and ensuring upstream cancel callback is only invoked once. Added unit tests covering cancel once semantics.

2025-02-28 Evan Liu (perf): Ran microbench against streaming toy workload — p95 token latency increased ~3.2% with adapter in Node; within target. Noted slight GC churn in allocation-heavy path; suggested small buffer reuse optimization.

2025-03-01 Asha Menon: Added docs stub and examples. Marking ticket In Progress and creating follow-up ENG-10024 to track bundler-targeted overload testing and publish notes for esbuild/rollup consumers.
